cards.text: Quick catch-up, friend. Samuel, Israel's prophet, has died, and all Israel mourned him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. Saul, Israel's king, has also removed something from the land.

cards.question: What has Saul removed from the land?

cards.text: Now the Philistines gather and camp at Shunem, and Saul gathers all Israel and camps at Gilboa. Two camps, two armies, and I bet NOBODY is sleeping well tonight.

cards.question: When Saul sees the Philistine army, he feels confident and ready to charge.

cards.text: Saul is afraid and trembles VIOLENTLY, the whole-body kind, like a phone on the table buzzing with forty group chat notifications. Then he inquires of the LORD.

cards.question: Saul is afraid and inquires of the LORD. How does the LORD answer him?

cards.text: No dreams. No Urim. No prophets. So Saul turns to his servants with a request.

cards.question: With no answer from the LORD, Saul tells his servants to find him a woman who is a ___ so he can go and consult her.

cards.text: "There is a medium at Endor," his servants reply. Hold on. Didn't Saul remove the mediums from the land? Somebody missed a spot.

cards.question: Before Saul heads to the medium at Endor, what does he do?

answers.text: He calls for Abiathar the priest

cards.text: In disguise, Saul sets out with two of his men, and they come to the woman at night. Saul says, "Consult a spirit for me. Bring up for me the one I name."

cards.question: The woman at Endor doesn't know who this stranger is. How does she answer his request?

answers.text: She asks why he set a trap to get her killed
She asks to be paid in silver first
She tells him to come back tomorrow

cards.question: Saul answers the woman by swearing to her by the LORD that no punishment will come upon her.

cards.text: Think about that, friend. The man who removed the mediums from the land is now swearing by the LORD to keep one safe.

cards.question: The woman asks whom she should bring up. Saul tells her to bring up ___.
When the woman sees Samuel, she stays calm and quiet.

cards.text: She cries out in a loud voice, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"
"Do not be afraid," the king replies, and he asks what she sees. "I see a god coming up out of the earth," the woman answers.

cards.question: Saul asks the woman what the figure looks like. What does she describe?

answers.text: An old man wearing a robe
A young man holding a spear
A tall man dressed in armor

cards.question: Once Saul knows it is Samuel, he bows facedown in reverence.

cards.text: Then Samuel speaks to Saul: "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?"
"I am deeply distressed," Saul replies. The Philistines are fighting against him, and God has turned away and no longer answers him by prophets or by dreams.

cards.question: Saul has called up Samuel. What does Saul want Samuel to do?

answers.text: Pray to the LORD for him

cards.text: Samuel asks why Saul is consulting him, since the LORD has turned away from Saul and become his enemy. Then Samuel says the LORD has done exactly what He spoke through Samuel.

cards.question: Samuel says the LORD has torn the kingdom out of Saul's hand. Who has the LORD given it to?
Why does Samuel say the LORD has torn the kingdom out of Saul's hand?

answers.text: Saul did not obey the LORD about Amalek
Saul refused to fight the Philistines
Saul took the priests' land for himself

cards.question: Samuel tells Saul that the LORD will deliver Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
Samuel tells Saul that tomorrow Saul and his ___ will be with Samuel.

cards.text: Immediately Saul falls flat on the ground, terrified by Samuel's words. And his strength is gone.

cards.question: Saul's strength is gone. What reason does the passage give?

answers.text: He had not eaten all day and night
He had been wounded in battle
He had been sick for many days

cards.text: The woman comes to Saul and sees how distraught he is. She reminds him that she took her life in her hands and did as he told her.

cards.question: Now the woman asks Saul to listen to her. What does she want to do for him?

answers.text: Set some bread before him to eat
Hide him in her house until morning
Bring up Samuel for him once more

cards.question: When the woman offers Saul food, he eats right away.
Saul says, "I will not eat." Who joins the woman in urging him?

cards.text: Saul listens, gets up from the ground and sits on the bed. Getting up after news like that is no small thing, and I say that as a guy who spent YEARS lying in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Saul is sitting on the bed at the woman's house. What does the woman do next?

answers.text: She sends his men out to find food
She tells him to rest until morning

cards.text: She quickly slaughters the fattened calf she had at her house, and she takes flour, kneads it and bakes unleavened bread. Somebody's KNEADING DOUGH in this story, and friend, now you've got my FULL attention.

cards.question: Saul and his servants eat, and then they stay at her house until morning.

cards.text: Saul and his men walk back out into the night. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is not done.

findings.problem: The setup joke 'I bet NOBODY is sleeping well tonight' signals that Saul is uneasy. That rules out the 'True' answer on card 4, which asks whether Saul feels confident and ready to charge.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'He does not answer him' stands out. Both wrong answers start with 'Through' and name a way the LORD answers, so the one answer shaped differently is the right one.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This story card only comments on the oath already told and answered on card 13 (28:10). It doesn't move the passage forward. It works as a recap of the irony from cards 2 and 9.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The woman's line "I see a god coming up out of the earth" is quoted before the card says who is speaking.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: Saul's line "I am deeply distressed" is quoted before the card says who is speaking.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Lead the army at Gilboa' isn't believable. Every card so far has shown Samuel as a dead prophet brought up from the earth, so asking him to lead troops reads as silly.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank takes Samuel's own line and blanks out the word 'sons'. The earlier cards give the baker no way to reason out sons over servants or wives, so the card tests wording they haven't seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The closing line copies the doc's example almost word for word: 'And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is not done.'

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
